20261201-A.finding: The valid candidate 1 improved the measured best from 11.34364 to 11.08646; the other valid proposal did not.

20261201-B.finding: Both proposals were valid but worse than the round-1 incumbent; retain the earlier verified source.

20261201-C.finding: The best improved slightly to 11.07732, keeping the far anchor but changing both savings weight and demand reward; a single-coefficient interpretation is unsupported.
20261201-C.hypothesis: Two changed coefficients prevent assigning the improvement to the savings weight alone.

20261201-D.finding: The candidate retained the start and savings sign but replaced adaptive coefficients with constants and added a radial term. It did not improve.
20261201-D.hypothesis: Preserving the sign alone did not reproduce the incumbent's adaptive ordering.

20261202-A.finding: Neither legal candidate improved the previous best. The round-1 source remains selected.

20261202-B.finding: Candidate 1 improved to 12.01258 and was selected. The second legal candidate was worse.

20261202-C.finding: The best improved to 11.72485, preserving the far start but rewriting the in-route score as detour, pull-home and capacity components. This did not test a small savings intercept change.
20261202-C.hypothesis: The accepted candidate is an empirical alternative, not evidence about the intercept-only hypothesis.

20261202-D.finding: The best retained the depot start and savings term, but converted an additive fill reward into a multiplicative factor. It was worse than the original incumbent.
20261202-D.hypothesis: The capacity transformation did not improve the fixed development suite.

20261203-A.finding: Candidate 2 improved the best to 11.67495. Both proposed candidates were valid.

20261203-B.finding: Candidate 1 improved the measured best to 11.82749. The two candidates passed validity.

20261203-C.finding: The best kept the nearest depot rule and main in-route score, changing linear capacity ratio to its square in the distance term. It improved to 11.09967.
20261203-C.hypothesis: Changing the effective demand-distance term is supported here, although the requested coefficient-only edit was not adopted literally.

20261203-D.finding: Candidate 2 kept the nearest start and main savings score, and changed the tight-capacity trigger from 2.5 to 3 times maximum feasible demand. It scored 11.28790, slightly worse than the incumbent.
20261203-D.hypothesis: The proposed threshold movement did not improve this suite.
